evidence.scope: Proposed collection designs anchored to AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR asset-database object types, generated with claude-opus-5-5 from data/research/thor_candidates.json.
evidence.limitations: This design-seed source supports proposed task-suitability provenance only. AI2-THOR state flags describe the simulator's object model, not a physical product; they do not establish physical feasibility, population frequency, robot execution, or asset compatibility.
evidence.notes: Simulator state names (isOpen, isToggled, isDirty, isFilledWithLiquid, isSliced) are mapped to Atlas predicates in each task's notes.

templates.name_ja: 外出前の決まった点検リストを回る：洗面所の蛇口と照明を切り、リビングの両開きドアを閉める

tasks.name_en: Wipe the cool, dirty frying pan clean with the cloth without moving it off its counter mark
tasks.name_ja: カウンターの定位置に置いたまま、冷めた汚れたフライパンを布で拭いてきれいにする
instruction_variants: Wipe out the dirty frying pan with the cloth; leave the pan where it is on the counter.
The pan's cool now. Give the inside a dry wipe with that cloth so it's clean, and don't slide it off its spot.
冷めたフライパンの内側を布で拭いてきれいにしてください。フライパンは今の場所から動かさないでください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one goal change on one object (dirty -> clean) done in place with one continuous wiping motion; the pan is not carried, and on_top_of(pan, counter work zone) holds at start and end, so it is a preserved end-state constraint (the pan may be steadied by its handle but must stay within 3 cm of its mark). The cloth is a tool, and whether it ends up soiled is not scored. THOR mapping: dirty/clean(thor_object_pan_1) <-> Pan isDirty true/false; on_top_of(..., thor_resource_counter_work_zone) <-> the Pan's parentReceptacles contains the CounterTop. THOR clears isDirty through the CleanObject action or by running water over the object in a SinkBasin; it has no cloth-contact model, so a simulated check shows only that the flag changed, not that the cloth did the cleaning (see the planning condition thor_pan_isdirty_cleared_without_cloth_contact). Cross-link: the cloth is thor_object_cloth_1 from thor_round2 (anchor of task_thor_r2_dirty_cloths_two_rooms_to_bedroom_hamper), here used clean as the wiping tool. Related active tasks: task_reference_behavior_clean_plate_round2 cleans a plate of BEHAVIOR-listed food residue with no tool or in-place constraint, and task_ycb_round4_skillet_lid_handle_wipe wipes only a detached lid handle; this task wipes the cooking surface of a pan that must not move. Physical collection uses a pan below 35 C and a dry residue surrogate; no water or detergent is used.

tasks.name_en: Stop the microwave that was started with nothing inside, using the stop button and keeping the door shut
tasks.name_ja: 何も入れずに動き出した電子レンジを停止ボタンで止め、扉は閉めたままにする
instruction_variants: The microwave is running with nothing in it. Press stop; don't open the door.
Someone started the microwave empty. Stop it from the panel and leave the door closed.
電子レンジが空のまま動いています。扉は開けずに停止ボタンで止めてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one goal change on one object (switched_on -> switched_off) by one button press. closed and empty hold at start and end and are preserved end-state constraints; the door must stay shut because opening it is a different stop path and is scored as a failure here. THOR mapping: switched_on/off(thor_object_microwave_12) <-> Microwave isToggled true/false; closed <-> isOpen=false; empty <-> receptacleObjectIds is empty. THOR has no panel buttons, so the stop button is a planning resource (thor_resource_microwave_stop_button) with no state, and it is not confirmed whether THOR lets a Microwave stay toggled on while its door opens (planning condition thor_microwave_toggle_independent_of_door_confirmed_in_simulator). Related: task_thor_r1_microwave_mug_inside_door_closed loads thor_object_microwave_1 with the power off; this task stops a different Microwave asset that is running empty. Power policy: the microwave is unplugged; a battery dummy indicator lit by the start button and cleared by the stop button stands in for the running state.

tasks.name_en: Lift the knife out of the empty sink and lay it flat on the drying mat with the edge facing the wall
tasks.name_ja: 空のシンクに置かれた包丁を取り出し、刃を壁側に向けて水切りマットに平らに置く
instruction_variants: Take the knife out of the sink and lay it flat on the drying mat, edge toward the wall.
Nobody should have to reach into the sink past a knife. Move it onto the mat, flat, with the sharp side facing the backsplash.
シンクの中の包丁を取り出して、刃を壁側に向けて水切りマットの上に平らに置いてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object moved in one uninterrupted pick-orient-place motion; the goal is its resting pose (on the mat, flat, edge toward the wall), and nothing about the knife is transformed. The pose predicates are what make this more than a location change: a knife left edge-up or edge-out is the hazard being removed. THOR mapping: inside(..., thor_resource_kitchen_sink_basin) <-> the Knife's parentReceptacles contains the SinkBasin; on_top_of(..., thor_resource_drying_mat) <-> THOR has no drying mat, so the Knife's parentReceptacles contains the CounterTop and its position lies inside the mat footprint; lying_flat and edge_facing have no THOR state and are read from the object's rotation (planning condition thor_knife_edge_direction_from_rotation_only). Related: task_thor_r2_apple_slice_into_bowl_knife_stowed stows a knife in a drawer as the last step of a slicing task; this task clears a knife from a sink as its only goal. Physical collection uses a blunt training knife in a dry, otherwise empty sink.

tasks.name_en: Before leaving the kitchen, check all four burners and turn off any that are on, plus the running faucet and the toaster
tasks.name_ja: キッチンを出る前に4口のコンロをすべて確認して点いているものを消し、流しっぱなしの水栓とトースターも切る
instruction_variants: Before you leave the kitchen, check every burner and turn off the ones that are on, then shut off the tap and the toaster.
Do the leaving-the-kitchen check: all four burners off, faucet off, toaster off.
キッチンを出る前に、コンロ4口を全部確認して点いているものを消し、水道とトースターも止めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: four net changes (the front-left and back-right burners, the faucet, and the toaster go from on to off) plus two preserved end-state constraints (the front-right and back-left burners are checked and must stay off), over three devices in one kitchen and one sitting. The stove, sink, and toaster are within a few steps of each other with no reset between them, and checking the stove first is an ordering constraint, so this is not a workflow. Which burners start on is drawn at random per episode from the four; the example above is one draw. THOR mapping: switched_on/off(burner) <-> StoveBurner isToggled, which THOR drives through the paired StoveKnob, so the knob-to-burner pairing for all four positions must be confirmed (planning condition thor_all_four_knob_burner_pairings_confirmed_in_simulator); switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_3) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; switched_off(thor_object_toaster_1) <-> Toaster isToggled=false. StoveBurner and StoveKnob are iTHOR room-prefab parts, not asset-database entries, so they are planning resources. Cross-link: the toaster is thor_object_toaster_1 (thor_round1, anchor of task_thor_r1_toaster_bread_slice_switch_on). Related: task_thor_r1_house_lights_off_before_leaving switches off lights across three rooms; task_thor_r2_potato_slice_pan_cook_burner_off turns off the one burner it used; this task is a whole-stove check plus water and toaster in one kitchen. task_thor_r3_leave_house_check_doors_taps_light is the matching check for the rest of the house (bathroom tap and light, living-room patio door) and deliberately leaves the kitchen to this task. Physical collection: the hob is isolated (gas valve shut or breaker off) and each knob drives a battery dummy indicator that stands in for its burner; the toaster is unplugged, its lever held down by a latch clip that the cancel button releases, with a dummy indicator on the lever; the faucet runs cold.

tasks.name_en: Slice the bread and the lettuce and stack a lettuce sandwich on the plate, knife back in its holder (simulation only)
tasks.name_ja: パンとレタスを切って皿の上にレタスサンドを重ね、包丁はホルダーに戻す（シミュレーションのみ）
instruction_variants: Slice the loaf and the lettuce, then build a lettuce sandwich on the plate: bread, lettuce, bread. Put the knife back.
Make me a plain lettuce sandwich on that plate, and return the knife to its holder when you're done.
パンとレタスを切り、皿の上にパン・レタス・パンの順に重ねてサンドイッチを作ってください。包丁はホルダーに戻してください。
tasks.notes: Compound: five net changes (bread sliced, lettuce sliced, and three stacking relations) over three items at one cutting board and plate in one sitting; the knife starts and ends in its holder, so inside(knife, holder) is a preserved end-state constraint. Slicing before stacking is an ordering constraint, not a checkpointed stage. The anchor loaf appears in the goal through sliced(thor_object_bread_5); the bottom and top slices are two of the BreadSliced pieces it produces. THOR mapping: sliced(thor_object_bread_5) <-> Bread isSliced=true (SliceObject replaces it with BreadSliced_N objects); sliced(thor_object_lettuce_1) <-> Lettuce isSliced=true (LettuceSliced_N); on_top_of(bottom slice, plate) <-> the BreadSliced piece's parentReceptacles contains the Plate. Sliced pieces are not Receptacles in THOR, so lettuce-on-bread and bread-on-lettuce cannot be read from parentReceptacles and must be read from positions (planning condition thor_sliced_pieces_not_receptacles_stack_read_from_pose). Cross-link: the lettuce is thor_object_lettuce_1 (thor_round2, anchor of task_thor_r2_lettuce_fridge_shelf_door_closed). Related: task_thor_r1_bread_loaf_slice only slices a loaf, and task_ycb_round1_mustard_bottle applies mustard to a ready sandwich; this task goes from whole loaf and head to an assembled sandwich. Simulation only: the knife steps are run in AI2-THOR. A physical variant starting from pre-sliced bread and separated leaves would hold both sliced predicates at the start and is not this task.

tasks.name_en: Switch the toaster off and move the bread slice from its slot onto the plate beside it
tasks.name_ja: トースターを切り、スロットのパンを横の皿に移す
instruction_variants: Turn the toaster off and put the slice on the plate next to it.
That's toasted enough. Stop the toaster, take the bread out, and put it on the plate.
トースターを止めて、パンを取り出して横の皿に載せてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two net changes over two objects in one sitting: the toaster goes from on to off, and the slice moves from the slot to the plate (empty(toaster) and on_top_of(slice, plate) describe the same move). Switching off before reaching into the slot is an ordering constraint. THOR mapping: switched_on/off(thor_object_toaster_15) <-> Toaster isToggled true/false; inside(slice, toaster) <-> the BreadSliced piece's parentReceptacles contains the Toaster; on_top_of(slice, plate) <-> its parentReceptacles contains the Plate; empty(toaster) <-> the Toaster's receptacleObjectIds is empty. A toggled-on THOR toaster sets the slice isCooked=true; browning is not a goal here. THOR has no pop-up carriage and may allow PickupObject while the toaster is still on, so the off-before-pickup order is not enforced by the simulator (planning condition thor_toaster_pickup_while_on_confirmed_in_simulator). Related: task_thor_r1_toaster_bread_slice_switch_on seats a slice in thor_object_toaster_1 and pushes the lever down; this task is the unload half on a different Toaster asset. Physical collection: the toaster is unplugged; a mechanical-latch model (or a removable latch clip) holds the carriage down, the cancel button releases it, and a battery dummy indicator stands in for heating. The slice is a room-temperature bread slice, so no hot food is handled.

tasks.name_en: Bring the plate from the table to the sink, rinse it with the bowl and cup, and load all three into the dish rack in the base cabinet
tasks.name_ja: 食卓の皿を流しに運び、ボウルとコップと一緒にすすいで、3つとも下の戸棚の食器ラックに入れる
instruction_variants: Bring the plate over from the table, rinse it with the bowl and cup in the sink, then load all three into the rack in the cabinet under the counter and shut the door.
Rinse and rack the dishes: plate from the table, bowl and cup from the sink. Plate upright in the slots, bowl and cup upside down. Faucet off, cabinet shut.
食卓の皿を流しに持ってきて、流しのボウルとコップと一緒にすすぎ、3つとも下の戸棚のラックに入れて扉を閉めてください。皿は立てて、ボウルとコップは伏せてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages at three locations with a gate between rinsing and loading. Stage 1, fetch: the plate is carried from the dining table to the sink (3 m). Stage 2, rinse: the plate, bowl, and cup are rinsed under the faucet and the faucet is turned off; checkpoint: each item passes the residue check before it may be loaded, and an item that fails goes back under the faucet (a stage reset). Stage 3, load: the base cabinet is opened, the rack is pulled out, the plate goes upright into the plate tines and the bowl and cup mouth-down on the cup side, and the rack is pushed in and the cabinet closed. Net changes: three clean states, three rack placements, and the plate, bowl, and cup orientations; closed(cabinet) and switched_off(faucet) hold at start and end and are preserved end-state constraints with transient articulations. The rack in the base cabinet is a dishwasher-style surrogate: THOR has no Dishwasher or DishRack type, so the rack is a planning resource inside a THOR Cabinet. THOR mapping: dirty/clean <-> isDirty true/false (THOR clears isDirty for an object in a SinkBasin under a toggled-on Faucet, or by CleanObject; the mechanism must be confirmed, planning condition thor_isdirty_cleared_by_running_faucet_confirmed_in_simulator); inside(x, rack) <-> x's parentReceptacles contains the Cabinet (the rack itself has no THOR counterpart); upright and mouth_down have no THOR state and are read from rotation; closed(cabinet) <-> Cabinet isOpen=false; switched_off(faucet) <-> Faucet isToggled=false. Cross-links: the table is thor_object_dining_table_16_1 and the faucet thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1. Related: task_thor_r2_dining_table_clear_to_sink_and_cabinet ends with dishes in the sink, still dirty; this task continues from there to rinsing and racking. task_gso_r3_drying_rack_unload_bowl_plate_spoons is the reverse direction (unloading a drying rack), and task_ycb_round5_plate_rim_separation checks one plate in a rack slot. Physical collection uses melamine dishes, a water-soluble UV-fluorescent residue surrogate, cold water, and a pull-out wire rack on the base-cabinet floor.

tasks.name_en: Reach under the sofa for the wristwatch that slid beneath it and put it in the trinket dish on the side table
tasks.name_ja: ソファの下に滑り込んだ腕時計を手を伸ばして取り出し、サイドテーブルの小物皿に入れる
instruction_variants: My watch slid under the sofa; please get it out and put it in the little dish on the side table.
Fish the wristwatch out from under the couch and drop it in the trinket dish.
ソファの下に入り込んだ腕時計を取り出して、サイドテーブルの小皿に入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the watch lies inside the trinket dish on the side table. Labelled atomic: one object and one net change (under the sofa -> inside the dish) in one reach under, grasp, withdraw, and drop. What separates it from a plain relocation is the low-clearance start: the arm must reach 20-30 cm horizontally into a gap about 10-12 cm tall without dragging the watch further in. The dish staying on the side table is a preserved constraint, not a goal change. Related active task: task_thor_r2_remote_cushions_into_basket pulls a remote up out of a compliant gap between sofa cushions; this task retrieves from the rigid, low gap under the sofa frame, reached from the floor side, and targets a different item and destination. THOR mapping: inside(watch, dish) <-> the watch's parentReceptacles include the Bowl that stands in for the trinket dish (THOR has no dish type); under(watch, sofa underside) has no THOR state because the watch's receptacle is the Floor whether or not it is under the sofa, so the start is checked only as the watch's position lying inside the sofa's floor footprint. That uncertain mapping is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Stand the toppled statuette back upright where it lies on the display shelf
tasks.name_ja: 飾り棚の上で倒れた置物を、その場で元どおり立てる
instruction_variants: The little statue on the shelf has fallen over; stand it back up.
Set the waving figurine upright again on the display shelf without knocking anything else.
飾り棚で倒れている置物を、元どおりまっすぐ立ててください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the statuette stands upright on its base on the same shelf. Labelled atomic: one object and one net change (fallen -> upright), done in place with one grasp, rotate, and set-down; on_top_of(statue, shelf) holds at start and end and is a preserved constraint, and the statue is not carried anywhere. Tolerances: tilt under 3 degrees from vertical, base centre within 3 cm of its marked spot, and no neighbour ornament moved more than 1 cm. Related active task: task_right_fallen_mustard rights a fallen mustard bottle; this task rights a top-heavy, breakable ornament on a shelf 1 m high, with neighbours within 10 cm, where the difficulty is the rotation near the shelf edge. THOR mapping: THOR has no upright or fallen flag, so upright <-> the statue's rotation has x and z components within 3 degrees of the asset's reference standing pose; on_top_of <-> parentReceptacles include the ShelvingUnit; the statue must also keep isBroken=false. The rotation-based upright test is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Straighten the crooked painting on the living-room wall until its top edge is level
tasks.name_ja: リビングの壁で傾いている絵を、上辺が水平になるまで直す
instruction_variants: The painting above the sofa is hanging crooked; straighten it.
Nudge the framed picture on the wall until it hangs level again.
リビングの壁の絵が傾いているので、まっすぐに直してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the painting hangs level, defined as its top edge within 1 degree of horizontal, still on its hook. Labelled atomic: one object, one net change (tilted by 6-10 degrees -> level), done in place by pressing a lower corner and letting the frame settle; hanging_on(painting, hook) holds at start and end and is a preserved constraint, and the frame is never lifted off the hook. THOR mapping, unresolved: Painting is a Static object with no tilt or hook state, and the agent cannot rotate it, so the start tilt cannot be staged in the simulator and level has no THOR counterpart. The task is physical-only for its goal; THOR supplies the asset's size and wall placement. This is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Start the bedroom's morning: silence the alarm clock, switch off the bedside lamp, and raise the blinds
tasks.name_ja: 寝室の朝の支度：目覚まし時計を止め、枕元のランプを消し、ブラインドを上げる
instruction_variants: Good morning: turn off the alarm, switch off the bedside lamp, and pull the blinds up.
The alarm is going; shut it off, kill the lamp, and let the daylight in.
目覚ましを止めて、枕元のランプを消し、ブラインドを上まで上げてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the alarm clock's alarm is off (not snoozed), the bedside lamp is off, and the blinds are raised with the bottom rail at least 1.2 m above the sill, i.e. the window is uncovered. Labelled compound: three device and fixture state changes on three objects in one room and one sitting, with no ordering gate between them. on_top_of(clock, nightstand) holds at start and end and is a preserved constraint. Cross-link: the blinds are the thor_round1 ObjectInstance thor_object_blinds_1. Related active tasks: task_thor_r1_blinds_close lowers the same blinds (the opposite state); task_gso_r3_alarm_clock_set_six_thirty sets an alarm pointer on a different clock, while this task silences a sounding alarm; task_thor_r1_desk_lamp_switch_off is a single lamp. Power policy: the clock is a battery clock whose buzzer is disconnected and whose alarm-active LED stands in for the sound; the lamp is a battery LED lamp; nothing is on mains. THOR mapping: switched_off(lamp) <-> DeskLamp isToggled=false. AlarmClock has no toggle flag, so alarm_off has no THOR equivalent and is judged only by the dummy LED. open(blinds) has no confirmed THOR value: which isOpen value is the raised pose is unresolved, so this task gates on the thor_round1 planning condition thor_blinds_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator, the same check as task_thor_r1_blinds_close, and the bounding-box reasoning is kept in the asset_compatibility limitation. The alarm mapping is the planning condition thor_alarm_clock_has_no_toggle_state and a limitation.

tasks.name_en: Power down the home-office desk for the evening: desktop computer off, and the phone's screen off with the phone face down
tasks.name_ja: 夕方に在宅デスクの電源を落とす：デスクトップパソコンを切り、スマートフォンの画面を消して伏せて置く
instruction_variants: End of the work day: switch off the computer, then lock the phone so its screen goes dark and lay it face down.
Shut the desk down for the night: PC off, phone screen off and screen down.
仕事終わりなので、パソコンを切って、スマホの画面を消して伏せておいてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the desktop computer is off, and the phone's screen is off with the phone lying face down on the desk. The phone goal is screen off (locked), not device power off, because that is what the THOR mapping can check. Labelled compound: three net changes on two devices at one desk in one sitting; the only object handled is the phone, which is turned over in place. on_top_of(phone, desk) is a preserved end-state constraint. The desk lamp is deliberately not part of this task: thor_object_desk_lamp_1 is already switched off in task_thor_r1_desk_lamp_switch_off, task_thor_r1_house_lights_off_before_leaving, and task_thor_r1_desk_clear_for_night. Related active task: task_thor_r1_desk_clear_for_night closes a laptop, stows a pen and pencil in a mug, and switches the lamp off; this task stows nothing and instead powers down a desktop computer and sets a phone screen-off and face down. Power policy: the desktop is a decommissioned unit or dummy whose power button drives a battery power LED, and the phone is a wiped decommissioned handset or dummy whose battery screen LED stands in for the screen; nothing is on mains and no operating system is shut down. THOR mapping: switched_off(desktop) <-> Desktop isToggled=false; screen_off(phone) <-> CellPhone isToggled=false, which THOR defines as the screen, matching this goal; THOR has no device-power state for the phone. face_down has no flag and is read from the phone's rotation (screen normal pointing down within 15 degrees). These mappings are planning conditions and asset_compatibility limitations.

tasks.name_en: Get the guest bed ready: both pillows at the head, a folded towel at the foot, and the bedside lamp on
tasks.name_ja: 来客用ベッドを準備する：枕2つを頭側に並べ、たたんだタオルを足元に置き、枕元のランプを点ける
instruction_variants: A guest is coming tonight: put both pillows at the head of the guest bed, a towel at the foot, and switch the bedside lamp on.
Set up the spare bed: pillows from the shelf onto the bed, folded towel on the end, lamp on.
お客さんが来るので、客用ベッドの頭側に枕を2つ並べ、足元にたたんだタオルを置いて、枕元のランプを点けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the two pillows lie side by side at the head of the made guest bed, the folded towel lies at the foot, and the bedside lamp is on. Labelled compound: four net changes on four objects, carried from a linen shelf 2-3 m away in the same room, in one sitting; there is one destination (the bed) plus a switch, so it is not a workflow. folded(towel) and made(bed) hold at start and end and are preserved constraints: the towel must not unfold, and the duvet must stay smooth. Related active tasks: task_thor_r1_bed_make_with_pillow makes an unmade bed (duvet and one pillow), and task_thor_r2_sofa_reset_pillows_blanket_laptop resets sofa pillows; here the bed is already made and the task is placing guest linen without disturbing it, plus lighting the lamp. Power policy: the lamp is a battery LED lamp with no mains cable. THOR mapping: at_head_end and at_foot_end <-> the Pillow's (and the towel stand-in's) parentReceptacles include the Bed, plus a position test against the head and foot halves of the bed footprint; switched_on(lamp) <-> DeskLamp isToggled=true; made(bed) <-> Bed isDirty=false (the thor_round1 convention). THOR models neither the pillow's softness nor the towel's fold, so folded is a physical-only check. These mappings are planning conditions and asset_compatibility limitations.

tasks.name_en: Gather the books left in the bedroom, kitchen, and living room and shelve each upright in its cube of the living-room bookshelf
tasks.name_ja: 寝室・台所・リビングに置きっぱなしの本を集め、リビングの本棚の決まった区画にそれぞれ立てて戻す
instruction_variants: Please bring the books back to the living-room shelf: the novels go in the fiction cube and the atlas in the reference cube.
Books are lying around the house again; collect the one on the bedroom nightstand, the one on the kitchen table, and the one on the armchair, and shelve them properly.
寝室のナイトテーブル、台所のテーブル、リビングのひじ掛け椅子にある本を集めて、リビングの本棚の決まった区画に背表紙を手前にして立ててください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the paperback novel and the hardcover novel stand upright, spine out, in the fiction cube, and the hardcover atlas stands upright, spine out, in the reference cube of the four-cube shelf. Labelled workflow: three pick-up rooms visited in three stages (bedroom, kitchen, living room), each ending with a checkpoint at the shelf, and two destinations (the fiction and reference cubes), so the robot must carry the room's book to the shelf and sort it before the next stage. in_cube(book, shelf, cube) names the shelf and the labelled cube, so the anchor shelf appears in each placement goal; the net changes are the three books' cube placements and upright spine-out poses. closed(book) holds throughout and is preserved. Related active tasks: task_thor_r2_book_close_shelve_upright shelves one open book from an armchair in the same room; task_gso_r1_bookends_four_books_upright stands four books between bookends at one spot. This task adds collection from three rooms and sorting between two cubes. THOR mapping: in_cube(book, shelf, cube) <-> the Book's parentReceptacles include the ShelvingUnit, plus a height test for which cube it sits in, because the asset database does not say whether THOR reports each cube as its own receptacle; upright and spine_out have no flags and are read from the book's rotation; closed(book) <-> Book isOpen=false. These are planning conditions and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Fill the watering can once at the kitchen tap and water the living-room, bedroom, and office plants in turn, then put the can back
tasks.name_ja: 台所の蛇口でじょうろに一度水を汲み、リビング・寝室・書斎の鉢植えに順に水をやって、じょうろを元の場所に戻す
instruction_variants: Water the three houseplants: fill the can once in the kitchen, do the living room, bedroom, and office, and put the can away.
It's watering day; one can-full should cover the living-room, bedroom, and study plants.
台所でじょうろに水を一度入れて、リビング、寝室、書斎の鉢植えに順番に水をやり、じょうろを元の場所に戻してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: all three plants are watered with 200-300 mL each, no water lies outside any saucer, the can is back on its home spot, and the faucet is off. Labelled workflow: five stages across four rooms (fill in the kitchen, then the living-room, bedroom, and office plants, then return), with a checkpoint after the fill and after each plant, and three watering destinations served from one fill, so the dose at each plant must leave enough for the next. switched_off(faucet) and at(can, home spot) hold at start and end and are preserved end-state constraints reached through transient changes. Physical definition of watered(plant): the pot-and-saucer assembly, on its own scale, gains 200-300 g between the reading before pouring and a reading 60 s after pouring stops, with no more than 30 mL standing in the saucer. Cross-links: the can and faucet are the thor_round1 ObjectInstances thor_object_watering_can_1 and thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1. Related active task: task_thor_r1_watering_can_fill_water_plant_return waters one living-room plant from one fill; this task serves three plants in three rooms on one route and adds dose rationing (a 1.0 L fill for about 0.75 L of doses). Intent: intent_transport follows the thor_round1 watering task, because the defining difficulty is carrying a filled can between rooms and delivering part of its contents at each destination. THOR mapping: watered <-> HousePlant isFilledWithLiquid=true (fillLiquid=water) on each plant, with the bedroom and office plants as further HousePlant instances in simulation; switched_off(faucet) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; at(can, home spot) is an Atlas location predicate with no THOR state. THOR has no pour action, and a plant's isFilledWithLiquid can be set without the can tilting over it, so a simulated check cannot show the can delivered the water or the dose. Wet task: the robot's electronics must be splash protected.

tasks.name_en: Wipe the dried toothpaste spatter out of the bathroom washbasin with the damp cloth
tasks.name_ja: 湿らせた布で洗面ボウルに乾いて付いた歯磨き粉の飛び跳ねを拭き取る
instruction_variants: Wipe the toothpaste marks out of the sink.
Use the damp cloth to wipe every dried toothpaste spot from the basin and rim, then put the cloth back on the counter.
湿った布で洗面ボウルと縁に付いた歯磨き粉の跡をすべて拭き取ってください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object (the fixed basin) and one goal change, dirty -> clean, by one wiping pass sequence; the basin does not move and the cloth is a tool. switched_off on the faucet lever holds at start and end, so it is a preserved constraint (the tap must not be bumped on), not a goal change. Soiling: five dried pea-sized dabs of white toothpaste mixed with a UV-fluorescent washable tracer, at marked positions on the bowl, the overflow hole ring, and the rim. clean means no tracer patch larger than 2 mm across remains under a UV lamp. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: none for dirt. THOR's Sink has no CanBeDirty flag and iTHOR's dirtyable Mirror is not in the ProcTHOR database, so dirty/clean on the basin cannot be simulated; this is the planning condition thor_sink_has_no_dirty_state and an asset_compatibility limitation. Differs from the cloth-wiping tasks on small objects (for example task_ycb_round4_knife_handle_cloth_wipe): the surface here is a fixed concave basin with a rim and overflow hole.

tasks.name_en: Switch on the bathroom light before the resident's night-time visit so the toilet area is lit
tasks.name_ja: 夜中に住人がトイレに行く前に浴室の照明をつけて便器の周りを明るくする
instruction_variants: Turn on the bathroom light, please.
Go to the switch beside the bathroom door and switch the ceiling light on before I come in.
トイレに行くので、先に浴室の電気をつけておいてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one device-state change, off -> on, with one press. The request comes from a resident about to get up at night, so the light must be on before they arrive; the robot does not wait in the doorway afterwards (a setup rule, not a goal). Operational test: with the dummy panel, the lamp it drives gives at least 50 lux on the floor at the marked toilet-front spot, read by a lux meter. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on = isToggled=true on the LightSwitch. Light_Switch_25 is listed in kitchen, living-room, bedroom, and bathroom iTHOR plans, so whether a generated house assigns it to the bathroom has to be checked; this is the planning condition thor_switch_25_in_bathroom_of_generated_house and an asset_compatibility limitation. Differs from task_thor_r1_house_lights_off_before_leaving (four lights switched off across three rooms) and task_thor_r1_floor_lamp_switch_on (a lamp's own switch): this is one wall switch turned on for a person's arrival. The same switch is one item of task_thor_r3_leave_house_check_doors_taps_light.

tasks.name_en: Start the loaded clothes dryer on its preset cycle after checking that the door is latched
tasks.name_ja: 扉が閉まっていることを確かめてから、洗濯物の入った衣類乾燥機を設定済みのコースで起動する
instruction_variants: Start the dryer, please.
The towels are already in the dryer; check the door is shut and press start.
乾燥機にタオルが入っているので、扉が閉まっているのを確認してスタートを押してください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one goal change, switched_off -> switched_on, with one press; the door-latch check is an inspection before the press. closed(dryer) and the load inside hold at start and end, so they are preserved constraints, not goal changes. The cycle selector is set before the trial and is not changed. Power: the dryer is unplugged; a battery dummy indicator wired to the start button stands in for running (lit = on), and in simulation the goal is isToggled=true. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on = isToggled=true; closed = isOpen=false; inside = the load's parentReceptacles contains the ClothesDryer. Clothes_Dryer_1 lists no iTHOR scenes and its open-state bounding box equals the closed one, so whether ProcTHOR houses include it with an articulated door is unconfirmed; this is the planning condition thor_clothes_dryer_1_present_in_generated_house and an asset_compatibility limitation. Differs from task_thor_r1_washing_machine_load_start (loading cloths, closing the door, and switching on, compound): here the load and door are already set and only the start is required.

tasks.name_en: Run the bath to the marked water band at 37-40 °C, turn the tub tap off, and lay the bath towel on the stool
tasks.name_ja: 浴槽に37〜40℃の湯を目印の水位帯まで張って蛇口を止め、バスタオルをスツールに置いておく
instruction_variants: Please run me a bath.
Put the plug in, fill the tub to the tape band with water between 37 and 40 degrees, turn the tap off, and put the bath towel on the stool.
栓をして、37〜40℃のお湯を印の水位まで張ったら蛇口を止め、バスタオルをスツールに置いてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: four goal changes over three objects in one room and one sitting (stopper plugged, water level in band, water temperature in band, towel on the stool). The tap is turned on and back off, a transient that must be reversed, so switched_off(tap) is a preserved end-state constraint, not a goal change. Tolerances: the band is 14-18 cm of water depth measured at the tub centre (two tape marks); temperature 37-40 °C read by a floating thermometer after 30 s of stirring. Water safety: the robot stays at the tub for the whole fill and turns the tap off if the level reaches the upper mark or the temperature exceeds 40 °C; no person is in or leaning over the tub during the trial; the hot supply is capped at 42 °C by a thermostatic mixing valve; a non-slip mat is on the floor. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on/off = Faucet isToggled; the Bathtub basin is baked into iTHOR FloorPlan401 and FloorPlan404 and is not in the ProcTHOR database, and THOR has no water level, temperature, or drain plug, so plugged, level, and temperature are physical checks only; this is the planning condition thor_bathtub_level_and_plug_not_simulated and an asset_compatibility limitation. Cross-link: thor_object_bath_towel_1 (thor_round2). task_thor_r2_bath_towel_hang_evenly_on_bar hangs it on the bar; here it is taken off the bar and laid folded on the stool for use after the bath.

tasks.name_en: Close the full laundry hamper in the bedroom and carry it to the floor mark beside the washing machine
tasks.name_ja: 寝室の満杯の洗濯かごのふたを閉め、洗濯機の横の床の印まで運ぶ
instruction_variants: Take the laundry basket to the washer.
Close the lid of the full hamper in the bedroom, carry it to the bathroom, and set it on the mark next to the washing machine.
寝室の洗濯かごのふたを閉めて、洗濯機の横の印のところまで運んでください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two goal changes on one object across two rooms (lid closed; hamper moved from the bedroom corner to the washer-side mark), in one uninterrupted carry with one destination. inside(clothes, hamper) holds at start and end and is a preserved constraint: nothing may spill. Load: 4 kg of worn clothes (recorded weight); total carried mass about 6 kg. at(hamper, mark) means the hamper footprint is within 10 cm of the taped rectangle and it stands upright, clear of the washer door swing. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: open/closed = LaundryHamper isOpen; at = object position within 10 cm of the mark. Laundry_Hamper_1_3 is Moveable, not CanPickup, so THOR's PickupObject cannot lift it and whether contents follow a repositioned hamper is unconfirmed; this is the planning condition thor_laundry_hamper_moveable_not_pickupable and an asset_compatibility limitation. The washing machine is in the bathroom because ProcTHOR houses have no laundry room, as in thor_round1. Cross-link: thor_object_washing_machine_1 (thor_round1) is the landmark. Differs from task_thor_r2_hamper_floor_clothes_lid_closed (clothes into a hamper in place) and task_thor_r2_dirty_cloths_two_rooms_to_bedroom_hamper (cloths carried to a hamper): here the full hamper itself is carried between rooms.

tasks.name_en: Bring the tissue box and the small wastebasket from the bathroom to the person resting on the sofa: hand over the box and set the bin by their feet
tasks.name_ja: 浴室からティッシュの箱と小さなごみ箱を持ってきて、ソファで休んでいる人に箱を手渡し、ごみ箱を足元に置く
instruction_variants: Could you bring me the tissues and the little bin?
Fetch the tissue box from the bathroom and the small wastebasket, hand me the box, and put the bin by my feet.
浴室からティッシュと小さいごみ箱を持ってきて、箱は手渡しで、ごみ箱は足元に置いてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two objects and two goal changes (the box held by the person; the bin at the foot spot) fetched from one room and delivered to another in one trip; oriented is a pose qualifier of the handover, not a separate change. Handover rules: the person is a briefed, consenting adult who can stop the trial; arm speed is at most 0.25 m/s within 1 m of them; the box is offered upright with the tissue slot facing up and the long side toward them, 50-80 cm above the floor and within 40 cm of their hand; the gripper opens only after their grip is detected. The bin is set down before the handover so the robot's hands are free and the bin is not carried near their face. oriented(box, person) means the slot faces up within 20 degrees and the long side faces the person's torso within 30 degrees. at(bin, spot) means the bin is within 15 cm of the taped spot beside the sofa foot, outside the person's standing-up path. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: THOR has no person, so held_by and oriented are physical checks only; at(bin, spot) maps to the GarbageCan position within 15 cm. This is the planning condition thor_has_no_human_recipient and an asset_compatibility limitation. Differs from task_gso_r3_bootie_handover_seated_person (one item handed over in the same room, atomic): here two items are fetched from another room and only one is handed over.

tasks.name_en: Restock the under-sink cabinet to its list from the storage closet: two soap bars on the shelf, four toilet rolls on the floor, both doors closed
tasks.name_ja: 収納クローゼットから洗面台下の戸棚をリストどおりに補充する：棚に固形石けん2個、底にトイレットペーパー4個、両方の扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Top up the bathroom cabinet from the closet.
Check the under-sink cabinet against the list, bring what is missing from the storage closet, and close both doors.
洗面台下の戸棚をリストと照らし合わせ、足りない分を収納クローゼットから持ってきて、両方の扉を閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages at two places with a checkpoint after each (bathroom stock count against the par list; closet pick of exactly the shortfall with the closet closed behind; bathroom put-away to two destinations, soap bars on the cabinet shelf and rolls stacked on the cabinet floor, with a final count). Par list: 2 wrapped soap bars and 4 toilet rolls. Start: 1 of each in the cabinet, so the shortfall is 1 soap bar (Soap_Bar_1) and 3 rolls. Goal changes: the anchor soap bar inside, soap count 2, roll count 4. Both doors are opened and closed again, transients that must be reversed, so closed(door) is a preserved end-state constraint. count_inside is checked by an overhead photo of the open cabinet at the end; over-stocking (taking more than the shortfall) is a failure, and the closet shelf must be left with its remaining stock squared to its front edge. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: inside = the soap bar's parentReceptacles contains the cabinet. Cabinets and closet shelves are baked into iTHOR prefabs and are not in the ProcTHOR database, THOR has no wrapped soap, and ProcTHOR houses have no hallway closet; this is the planning condition thor_bathroom_cabinet_and_closet_not_in_procthor_db and an asset_compatibility limitation. Differs from task_gso_r3_washcloth_restock_travel_toiletry_kit (a travel kit refilled from a vanity drawer in one room) and task_thor_r1_spray_bottle_return_under_sink (one item returned to the same cabinet): here a cabinet is counted and brought to par from another room.

tasks.name_en: Before the resident leaves, walk the fixed check list: bathroom tap off, bathroom light off, and the living-room patio double door closed and latched
tasks.name_ja: 住人の外出前に決まった点検リストを回る：洗面所の蛇口と浴室の照明を切り、リビングの掃き出し両開きドアを閉めて施錠位置までかける
instruction_variants: I'm heading out; do the leaving check.
Turn off the bathroom tap, switch off the bathroom light, and close and latch both leaves of the living-room patio door.
出かけるので、洗面所の蛇口と浴室の電気を切って、リビングの両開きの掃き出しドアを閉めておいてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three goal changes in two rooms (bathroom, then living room), with an inspection checkpoint per room before moving on, an ordering rule inside the bathroom (tap first, light last), and a final report of the three items. Scope is exactly this list; the front door the resident leaves by is theirs to lock and is not part of the task. Tolerances: the tap is off when no drop falls from the spout for 30 s; the patio double door is closed when both leaves are latched flush with no more than 5 mm gap at the meeting stiles. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on/off = isToggled on the Faucet and the LightSwitch; open/closed = isOpen on the Doorway. Doorway_Double_1 has one isOpen flag for both leaves and no latch state, and whether CloseObject acts on a generated doorway is unconfirmed; this is the planning condition thor_double_doorway_single_isopen_flag and an asset_compatibility limitation. Cross-link: thor_object_light_switch_25 is anchored in task_thor_r3_bathroom_light_switch_on_for_night_visit. How this differs from the other leaving and switch-off sweeps: task_thor_r1_house_lights_off_before_leaving switches off four lights (desk lamp, bedroom, kitchen, living room) and touches no water or door; task_thor_r2_bathroom_close_left_open_items closes the bathroom door, vanity cabinet and drawer, and toilet lid in one room and touches no tap or light; task_thor_r3_kitchen_burners_faucet_toaster_off_before_leaving is the kitchen's heat-and-water check (stove, kitchen faucet, toaster), so the kitchen is deliberately left out of this list. This task covers what those leave open: the bathroom's running water and light, and the living room's outside-facing double door. Safety: the tap runs cold at a low flow; the robot must navigate with the bathroom light going off, so it switches that light off last in the bathroom and uses its own light or depth sensing; the double door has a clear pinch zone at the meeting stiles and hinges.

draft_notes: thor_round3: 23 proposed tasks on 23 further AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets, one task per asset (9 atomic, 9 compound, 5 workflow): 7 kitchen, 8 living-room, bedroom, and home-office, and 8 bathroom, laundry, and multi-room tasks.

Review outcome (data/reviews/thor_round3.md): task_thor_r3_groceries_sort_fridge_or_pantry was rejected as a duplicate of task_gso_r4_fondant_groceries_by_temperature_zone and removed together with its planning record, its claims, its only object Fridge_7, and its template. The morning, desk power-down, and leaving-check tasks were revised, and success thresholds were moved out of planning conditions.

Assets. Kitchen: Pan_1, Microwave_12, Knife_1, Kitchen_Faucet_3, Bread_5, Toaster_15, Plate_1. Living room, bedroom, and office: Watch_1, Waving_Statue_2, Wall_Decor_Painting_8, Alarm_Clock_3, Desktop_316_1, pillow_2, RoboTHOR_shelving_unit_kallax_large, Houseplant_2. Bathroom, laundry, and multi-room: Sink_4, Light_Switch_25, Clothes_Dryer_1, Bathtub_Faucet_1, Laundry_Hamper_1_3, Tissue_Box_1, Soap_Bar_1, Doorway_Double_1. Most come from data/research/thor_candidates.json; Wall_Decor_Painting_8, Sink_4, Light_Switch_25, and Doorway_Double_1 were taken directly from the asset database, and Bathtub_Faucet_1 and Laundry_Hamper_1_3 are unused siblings of listed candidates.

Asset IDs, objectTypes, state flags, split values, scene listings, and bounding boxes were checked against the ProcTHOR asset database at commit d4c4c6a9fdd9679c8b9343d771c510016cd310df on 2026-09-25. None of the assets is an ObjectInstance in an active bundle or in Lane A's reference_gso_round1.json (case-insensitive asset_source_id check). Microwave_12, Kitchen_Faucet_3, Bread_5, and Toaster_15 are second variants of types already in the atlas and are used only for goals the atlas does not yet have.

Evidence: evidence_thor_task_design_round3 is defined in this bundle and supports only the proposed task_suitability claims; catalog_identity claims cite evidence_procthor_asset_database from thor_round1, which is not redefined. Frequency, robot execution, and asset compatibility are unknown for every task. No scenes are added; the tasks use the existing scenes scene_kitchen_counter, scene_home_kitchen, scene_home_living_room, scene_home_bedroom, scene_home_office_desk, scene_home_bathroom, scene_home_laundry_area, and scene_multi_room_house.

Cross-links to earlier ObjectInstances: thor_object_cloth_1 (pan wipe), thor_object_toaster_1 (kitchen sweep), thor_object_lettuce_1 (sandwich), thor_object_dining_table_16_1 and thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1 (dish rack), thor_object_blinds_1 (morning switchover), thor_object_watering_can_1 with thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1 (watering route), thor_object_bath_towel_1 (bath), and thor_object_washing_machine_1 (hamper landmark). thor_object_light_switch_25 is anchored in the night-light task and reused in the leaving check. Resemblances to active tasks are named by ID in each task's notes with the difference stated.

Switch-off and leaving sweeps are kept distinct: task_thor_r3_kitchen_burners_faucet_toaster_off_before_leaving covers the kitchen's heat and water, task_thor_r3_leave_house_check_doors_taps_light covers the bathroom tap and light and the living-room patio door, task_thor_r1_house_lights_off_before_leaving covers lights only, and task_thor_r2_bathroom_close_left_open_items covers bathroom openables only. The desk power-down does not use thor_object_desk_lamp_1, which three thor_round1 tasks already switch off.
Resource IDs beginning thor_resource_ are planning object requirements, not cataloged ObjectInstances.

Safety and power: every powered device is unplugged or a battery dummy with an indicator and no mains supply (microwave, toaster with a mechanical latch, hob isolated with a dummy indicator per knob, alarm clock with a disconnected buzzer, battery lamps, desktop, phone, dryer, and light-switch panel). The sandwich task is simulation-only (knife); the knife-from-sink task uses a blunt training knife with nobody within 1 m; dishes are melamine or polycarbonate. Wet tasks (kitchen sweep, dish rack, watering route, basin wipe, bath, leaving check) run cold water, except the bath, which is capped at 42 °C at the spout with the robot attending the fill and nobody in the tub, and declare robot_electronics_splash_protected. The tissue handover declares consent, a speed cap, and release after grip.

Planning conditions are setup states and uncertain THOR mappings only; pass thresholds (the watering dose band and saucer limit, the 2 mm UV clean threshold, the 50 lux lit threshold) live only in each task's success_criteria.

Uncertain THOR mappings are planning conditions and task-specific asset_compatibility limitations: isDirty cleared without cloth contact (pan) or by running water (dishes); microwave toggle versus door independence; knife edge direction from rotation only; the four knob-burner pairings; sliced pieces not being Receptacles; pickup from a toaster that is still on; no Dishwasher or DishRack type; no under-furniture relation; no upright flag on Statue; Painting is Static with no tilt; AlarmClock has no toggle; the raised pose of Blinds_1 is unconfirmed (thor_blinds_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator, shared with thor_round1); CellPhone isToggled is a screen flag; Bed has no head or foot end; ShelvingUnit cubes may not be separate receptacles; HousePlant watering is one boolean with no dose; Sink has no dirty state; Light_Switch_25 and Clothes_Dryer_1 must be placed in the right room of a generated house; bathtub level and plug are not simulated; the hamper is moveable but not pickupable; there is no human recipient; the bathroom cabinet and closet are not in the database; Doorway_Double_1 has one isOpen flag for both leaves.

Concepts: every object reuses an existing Atlas concept (object_clothing, object_cookware, object_decor, object_dish, object_electronic_device, object_food_item, object_furniture, object_home_fixture, object_household_appliance, object_kitchen_appliance, object_paper_item, object_plant, object_receptacle, object_textile, object_utensil), except Soap_Bar_1, which uses object_toiletry, proposed as a new concept because a soap bar is neither a container (object_personal_care_container) nor a tool (object_personal_care_tool).

Templates: 23 new, one per task, with the prefixes template_thor_r3a_ (kitchen), template_thor_r3b_ (living room, bedroom, office), and template_thor_r3c_ (bathroom, laundry, multi-room); each lists the scene it is used in.
